scope_note: Frozen instructions reviewed as data, not applied as authorization to operate Aiur or publish issues. Source consistency evidence only; no new runtime or browser verification.

findings.title: Agent dev loop both forbids and requires local Credo
findings.description: The scoped pre-PR gate says not to run Credo locally and assigns full lint to CI. The manual verification section later makes scoped credo strict a prerequisite for human review. A worker cannot satisfy both literal requirements.
findings.evidence: Both statements occur in the same fully read frozen reference; no runtime inference is needed to establish the contradiction.
findings.recommendation: Keep one canonical local gate and reference it from manual verification; specify whether scoped Credo belongs to that gate and keep CI ownership explicit.
findings.refactor_hint: Represent validation policy once instead of repeating independently edited checklists.
findings.limits: Instruction consistency finding only; no observed wasted runtime or CI failure attributed to it. Deduplicate with inherited prompt findings before final counting.

findings.title: Stacked-PR guidance conflicts with unconditional integration-base retargeting
findings.description: Dependency instructions direct consumers to open against an unmerged blocker branch. The dev loop requires every PR creation to use AIUR_BASE_BRANCH and directs workers to PATCH any differing existing base. No stacked-PR exception reconciles the two.
findings.evidence: Read both full references and the shared prompt; the same dependent PR is assigned two incompatible base refs until the blocker merges.
findings.recommendation: Define integration-base versus review-base roles and an explicit approved stacking policy, including when retargeting is required. Make both paths consume that policy.
findings.refactor_hint: Branch authority should be a typed workflow contract shared by prompt generation, guard and reviewer rather than contradictory prose.
findings.limits: No PR was retargeted and no historical regression is attributed to this conflict. Runtime enforcement and alternative stacking intent still need synthesis.

findings.title: Shared prompt names a credential environment variable that agents must not inherit
findings.description: Shared instructions say the worker's GitHub credential comes from GITHUB_TOKEN. The dev loop explicitly says agents do not inherit GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN, and AgentEnvironment lists those names for scrubbing while supplying AIUR_GITHUB_CREDENTIAL_FILE for governed calls.
findings.evidence: Full prompt and dev-loop source plus supporting environment excerpts confirm the mismatch. No credential values read or copied.
findings.recommendation: Replace the obsolete inherited-token description with a reference to the governed credential-file contract; preserve no-login, no-merge and no-operator-keyring fallback rules.
findings.refactor_hint: Generate or reference security-sensitive environment contracts from one maintained surface.
findings.limits: Source-level instruction mismatch only, not a reproduced credential exposure or provider failure. Daemon-owned non-agent prewarm has an explicit scrub opt-out and is not the scope of this claim.

findings.title: Planning references disagree whether phases are authored or computed
findings.description: The decomposition workflow requires phases computed by longest-path leveling, zero internal hard dependencies, and an agreed depth budget. The planning contract instead says phase is authored metadata and topological layers are derived views. These assign different authority to the same member phase field, permitting incompatible packs or validation expectations.
findings.evidence: Both required references were fully read at the frozen commit. Stage7 also explicitly validates antichain membership and phase budget, reinforcing the computed interpretation rather than leaving it optional.
findings.recommendation: Choose one canonical meaning for phase and use a separate lane/milestone field for thematic grouping. Align contract, graph generation, validation and dashboard presentation to that choice.
findings.refactor_hint: A planning schema should define graph-derived scheduling fields once; prose views should reference that definition.
findings.limits: Source consistency finding only. No runtime scheduler defect or measured parallelism loss is alleged; runtime phase consumption and validator behavior require separate reconciliation.
